To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stellar populations in the outer disks of spiral galaxies are dominated by a young population of stars, that the stellar populations at all radii of dwarf spheroidal galaxies are dominated by an old population of stars, and that the stellar populations of the outer regions of elliptical galaxies are also dominated by an old stellar population.

the stellar populations of Local Group galaxies have been studied extensively, but that we need to extend these studies to the full range of Local Universe galaxy types, and to do so we must have the observational capabilities to study resolved stellar populations in the outskirts of galaxies, and to study the more crowded regions in nearby galaxies.
the resolved stellar populations in galaxies can be used to reconstruct their star formation and chemical enrichment histories.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the resolved stellar populations in galaxies.
the formation and assembly of galaxies, and the formation and evolution of stars.

the study of resolved populations of stars in Local Group galaxies and nearby galaxies, to understand how and when galaxies assembled their stellar populations, to determine the star formation histories of the different components of galaxies, to determine how the chemical evolution of galaxies varies with environment and morphology, and to understand the role of stellar populations in the formation and evolution of galaxies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we will be able to determine the detailed star formation histories of a large number of galaxies, and thus be able to test our current models of galaxy formation and chemical evolution, and to provide constraints for the next generation of simulations.

the study of the history of star formation in galaxies has been revolutionized by the advent of the Hubble Space Telescope and the development of the HST/ACS, which has enabled a wide range of investigations of resolved stellar populations in galaxies, and will continue to do so with the HST/WFC3.
the history of star formation in galaxies is the most fundamental aspect of galaxy formation and the key to the evolution of galaxies and of the universe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to determine the star formation history of galaxies in a way that is consistent with their observed morphology and chemical composition.
we have obtained the first complete picture of the formation and evolution of a galaxy.

we will be able to determine the star formation histories and metallicities of galaxies as a function of galaxy mass, morphology and environment, and to understand the processes that have shaped them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of the Milky Way and other disk galaxies has proceeded in a remarkably uniform fashion.
galaxies are complex and dynamic entities, and that the assembly of the galaxy population in the universe is a complex and dynamic process that is still not fully understood.
galaxies are built by the accretion of smaller building blocks, but that the process is more complicated than simply adding the stars from each accreted system to the host galaxy.
